applied.problem: A steam engine's direction is set by its valve gear, so turning it off dead centre does not make it run either way; and not all locomotives are two-cylinder with quartered cranks (three-cylinder engines are 120 degrees apart).
The size of the split-phase angle is contested (about 30 degrees in some sources, about half of 90 in another, 25 in a worked example); 'about 30° in a typical motor' states one figure as settled.

'Up to about 250 W' reads as a hard limit where the source says the arrangement serves well up to 1/3 hp; the Read's 'the field now only pulses' is true only of the windings' field; and with the main open the switch would reclose as it slows, so 'could not keep running' is too absolute.

The practice's meter readings (main 4.5, start 15 ohm) clash unexplained with the picture's example winding values (15 and 36 ohm); and a running motor's real field is not purely pulsing, as the picture's main-winding-only arrow shows.
'The start winding burns out' is absolute; the source says it may overheat and fail.
'Burn it out' is absolute; the sources say the winding may overheat and fail, or can be damaged.
'Up to about 250 W' reads as a hard limit; the source says the arrangement serves well up to 1/3 hp (250 W).
